newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen dulled by U.S. Memorial Day.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen dulled by U.S. Memorial Day.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa was seen likely to pause Monday during the U.S. Memorial Day holiday, with prices moving aimlessly after a steady two-week climb, dealers said.

"Nothing much will happen today because of the Wall Street holiday," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox traders. "Beyond that, the bolsa will struggle to move higher in the near term after its recent strong advance, but the trend is clearly positive."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV posted its tenth consecutive gain Friday, rising 0.3 percent to 767.67 and stretching gains in the past two weeks to 6.1 percent.
Traders said the market was underpinned by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to touch interest rates last week and also by strong local industrial production data.
"The economy is growing at a quick pace which means we should see rising revenues," Diz said.
Local stocks were also favored by the apparent seven percent ceiling for U.S. long bond yields.
"The yield stayed below that key barrier which is a good sign," a trader said. He predicted that after Monday's lull floor volume would recover to a strong 30 million pesos.
